findings.acceptance: NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, non-TTY and unsupported-color terminals emit no ANSI control codes
findings.summary: ANSI support detection treats any TTY except TERM=dumb or NO_COLOR as color-capable.
findings.detail: When TERM is empty or identifies a terminal without ANSI support, supports_ansi_color still returns true and render_fd_list wraps state and priority fields in escape sequences.
findings.requested_change: Detect terminal color capability reliably and use plain text when support is absent or unknown.

findings.acceptance: Terminal list displays readable aligned columns
findings.summary: ANSI sequence width is overcounted by two columns for the current two-digit color codes.
findings.detail: ansi_color adds an opening sequence of len(code)+3 characters and a four-character reset, so the actual overhead is len(code)+7. The width adjustment adds len(code)+9, shifting body columns relative to headers.
findings.requested_change: Calculate the actual ANSI sequence overhead or compute alignment from visible text.
